# Company mapping database

Two layers. **Links** (config/companies.yaml): which operational indicators drive which company, segment and line item, with the expected timing and the channel, written before any model was fitted. **Profiles** (config/profiles/): segments, geographic exposure, customers, backlog, pricing and margin drivers, each supported by sentences quoted from the company's latest annual report. Every quote is checked against the filing text by `python -m indintel verify-mapping` and the test suite.

## Caterpillar Inc. (CAT)

Caterpillar makes construction and mining machinery, engines, turbines, locomotives and related parts and services, sold mainly through an independent dealer network, and also runs a captive finance business.

Source: [10-K filed 2026-02-13](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/18230/000001823026000008/cat-20251231.htm)

**Segments**

- **Construction Industries**: Machinery for infrastructure and building construction applications. Demand: Heavy and general construction, rental, quarry and aggregates, and mining
- **Resource Industries**: Surface and underground mining equipment, work tools, machinery components, wear and maintenance parts, plus fleet management, autonomy and safety technology and services. Demand: Mining (copper, iron ore, coal, oil sands, gold), heavy construction, quarry and aggregates
- **Power & Energy**: Reciprocating engines, turbines and turbine-related services, electric power generation systems, locomotives and rail products and services. Demand: Oil and gas, power generation (including data center applications), marine, rail and industrial applications
- **Financial Products**: Retail and wholesale financing, insurance and risk management products through Cat Financial and Insurance Services. Demand: Caterpillar customers and dealers purchasing or leasing Caterpillar equipment

**Geographic exposure.** Sales are worldwide, through 41 US and 109 non-US dealers serving 190 countries. In 2025 North America sales rose 6 percent and EAME 4 percent, while Asia/Pacific fell 2 percent; absolute regional dollar amounts are not quoted here.
> We distribute our machines principally through a worldwide organization of dealers (dealer network), 41 located in the United States and 109 located outside the United States, serving 190 countries.
>
> North America sales increased 6 percent due to higher sales volume, partially offset by unfavorable price realization.
>
> EAME sales increased 4 percent mainly due to higher sales volume and favorable currency impacts related to the euro, partially offset by unfavorable price realization.
>
> Asia/Pacific sales decreased 2 percent primarily due to unfavorable currency impacts related to the Australian dollar, and lower sales volume.
>

**Customers.** Machines are sold principally through independent dealers; engines also go to other manufacturers (OEMs) and through distributors; turbines and locomotives are sold directly to end customers by company sales forces.
Concentration: not disclosed.
> We sell finished products primarily through an independent dealer network and directly to OEMs and are subject to risks relating to their inventory management decisions and operational and sourcing practices.
>
> We sell some products, primarily turbines and locomotives, directly to end customers through sales forces employed by the company.
>

**Order backlog.** Backlog believed to be firm rose to $51.2 billion, with increases across the primary segments and the largest in Power & Energy.
Latest: $51.2 billion at December 31, 2025 (vs $30.0 billion at December 31, 2024).
Horizon: About $31.9 billion (roughly 62%) expected to be filled in 2026, derived as $51.2 billion less $19.3 billion not expected to be filled in 2026.
> The dollar amount of backlog believed to be firm was approximately $51.2 billion at December 31, 2025 and $30.0 billion at December 31, 2024.
>
> Of the total backlog at December 31, 2025, approximately $19.3 billion was not expected to be filled in 2026.
>
> Compared with year-end 2024, the order backlog increased across the primary segments, with the largest increase in Power & Energy.
>

**Pricing dynamics.** Price realization was unfavorable in 2025 (including in North America and EAME); the company expects favorable price realization of about 2 percent of sales and revenues in 2026. Higher tariffs were reflected in manufacturing costs.
> The strong backlog coupled with healthy end markets supports our expectations for sales volume growth in all three primary segments, as well as favorable price realization of about 2 percent of sales and revenues.
>
> The decrease was mainly due to unfavorable manufacturing costs and unfavorable price realization, partially offset by the profit impact of higher sales volume.
>

**Margin drivers.** Operating profit margin fell to 16.5 percent in 2025 from 20.2 percent, driven by unfavorable manufacturing costs (largely tariffs) and unfavorable price realization, partly offset by higher volume. The company expects tariff impact of about $2.6 billion in 2026.
> Operating profit margin was 16.5 percent in 2025, compared with 20.2 percent in 2024.
>
> Unfavorable manufacturing costs largely reflected the impact of higher tariffs.
>
> Based on the incremental tariffs announced in 2025 and in place by January 29, 2026, we expect the impact from tariffs to be around $2.6 billion in 2026, which is $800 million higher than incurred in 2025.
>

## Vertiv Holdings Co (VRT)

Vertiv designs, manufactures, installs and services critical digital infrastructure (power, thermal and related hardware, software and services) primarily for data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial environments.

Source: [10-K filed 2026-02-13](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1674101/000167410126000008/vrt-20251231.htm)

**Segments**

- **Americas**: Critical digital infrastructure hardware, software and services. Demand: Data centers, communication networks, commercial and industrial customers in the Americas
- **Asia Pacific**: Critical digital infrastructure hardware, software and services. Demand: Data centers, communication networks, commercial and industrial customers in Asia Pacific
- **Europe, Middle East & Africa**: Critical digital infrastructure hardware, software and services. Demand: Data centers, communication networks, commercial and industrial customers in EMEA

**Geographic exposure.** Segments are geographic. 2025 net sales of $10,229.9 million were 62% Americas, 20% Asia Pacific and 18% EMEA (about $6.39B, $2.02B and $1.82B excluding intercompany sales).
> We manage our business across three reportable segments based on our main geographic regions
>
> of which 62% was transacted in the Americas; 20% was transacted in Asia Pacific; and 18% was transacted in Europe, Middle East & Africa.
>
> Excluding intercompany sales, net sales were $6,386.3 in the Americas, $2,019.2 in Asia Pacific and $1,824.4 in Europe, Middle East & Africa.
>

**Customers.** Customers are data center, communication network and commercial and industrial operators, reached directly and through channel partners, distributors, IT resellers and value-added retailers.
Concentration: not disclosed.
> We design, manufacture and service critical digital infrastructure technology primarily for data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial environments.
>
> We also utilize a robust network of channel partners, distributors, IT resellers, and value-added retailers.
>

**Order backlog.** Backlog roughly doubled year over year; the filing cautions it is not necessarily indicative of future net sales.
Latest: $15.0 billion combined order backlog at December 31, 2025 (vs $7.2 billion at December 31, 2024).
Horizon: Majority considered firm and expected to ship within the next 12 to 18 months (no exact share).
> estimated combined order backlog was approximately $15.0 billion and $7.2 billion, respectively.
>
> The majority of the combined backlog as of December 31, 2025 is considered firm and is expected to be shipped within the next 12 to 18 months.
>
> The backlog consists of product and services for which a customer purchase order or purchase commitment has been received and which has not yet been delivered.
>

**Pricing dynamics.** The company is advancing a pricing plan and notes that, because of its large backlog, pricing changes take longer to show in results. Competition is on reliability, quality, price, service and relationships; tariffs and input costs have risen.
> We continue to take action to enhance our supply chain, such as qualifying new suppliers, and advancing our pricing plan.
>
> Also, due to our large backlog, pricing changes may take longer to be reflected in our financial results.
>
> In the past few years, we experienced significant increases in material, freight and labor costs and custom duties and tariffs.
>

**Margin drivers.** Consolidated gross margin was 36.3% in 2025 vs 36.6% in 2024. The filing names operational leverage, cost improvement actions and geographic mix as drivers of a segment margin increase, and product/service mix, inefficiencies and capacity build-out as drivers of margin erosion in another.
> Gross profit was $3,715.2 in 2025, or 36.3% of sales, compared to $2,934.2, or 36.6% of sales in 2024.
>
> Margin increased primarily driven by operational leverage, cost improvement actions, and geographical mix.
>
> Margin erosion was primarily due to the mix of product and service sales, operational inefficiencies, and increased capacity to support future global demand.
>

## Eaton Corporation plc (ETN)

Eaton makes electrical products and systems, aerospace fluid and filtration systems, and vehicle and eMobility components for data center, utility, industrial, commercial, residential, aerospace and mobility markets.

Source: [10-K filed 2026-02-26](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm)

**Segments**

- **Electrical Americas**: Electrical and industrial components, power distribution and assemblies, power quality, wiring devices, circuit protection, utility power distribution and services, primarily produced and sold in North and South America. Demand: Data center, utility, industrial, commercial and residential
- **Electrical Global**: Similar electrical and industrial components, power distribution, power quality and services, produced and sold primarily outside North and South America, plus hazardous duty electrical equipment. Demand: Data center, utility, industrial, commercial outside the Americas
- **Aerospace**: Aerospace fuel, hydraulics and pneumatic systems for commercial and military use, and filtration systems for industrial applications. Demand: Commercial and military aircraft manufacturers and aftermarket customers
- **Vehicle**: Drivetrains, powertrain systems and critical components for cars, light trucks and commercial vehicles. Demand: Automotive, commercial vehicle, aftermarket and off-road (to be combined with eMobility as Mobility, with a spin-off announced for 2027)
- **eMobility**: Mechanical, electrical and electronic components and systems for power management in on-road and off-road vehicles. Demand: Vehicle OEMs

**Geographic exposure.** Net sales are measured by destination. In 2025 the United States was $17,122 million of $27,448 million total, with Europe $5,078 million, Asia Pacific $2,704 million, Latin America $1,461 million and Canada $1,083 million (per the geographic table).
> Net sales are measured based on the geographic destination of sales.
>
> services that are primarily produced and sold in North and South America.
>

**Customers.** Sales go through distributors, resellers and manufacturers representatives and directly to OEMs, utilities and other end users.
Concentration: No single customer represented greater than 10% of net sales in 2025, 2024 or 2023.
> A significant portion of open orders placed with Eaton are by customers of electrical products and electrical system and services, original equipment manufacturers or distributors.
>
> No single customer represented greater than 10% of net sales in 2025, 2024 or 2023, respectively.
>

**Order backlog.** Backlog counts only orders to which customers are firmly committed; about 69% is targeted for delivery within twelve months.
Latest: approximately $19.8 billion at December 31, 2025.
Horizon: approximately 69% targeted for delivery in the next twelve months.
> Using this criterion, total backlog at December 31, 2025 was approximately $ 19.8 billion.
>
> At December 31, 2025, approximately 69 % of this backlog is targeted for delivery to customers in the next twelve months and the rest thereafter.
>
> In measuring backlog of unsatisfied or partially satisfied obligations, only the amount of orders to which customers are firmly committed are included.
>

**Pricing dynamics.** The filing does not quantify price effects in the text searched. It says suppliers are raising prices and that Eaton tries to recoup costs through pricing, but price increases could hurt market share or distributor relationships.
> Some of our suppliers have experienced the same conditions and, in response, have continued to increase their prices in response to increases in their costs of raw materials, energy, and/or labor.
>
> In addition, our responses to mitigate the impact of these conditions, such as potential price increases, could negatively impact our market share or relationships with distributors or customers.
>

**Margin drivers.** Gross margin fell to 37.6% in 2025 from 38.2%, with a 280 bp drag from commodity and wage inflation and 50 bp from acquisition and divestiture charges, offset by a 260 bp benefit from higher sales (volume leverage).
> Gross profit margin decreased from 38.2% in 2024 to 37.6% in 2025.
>
> Material factors affecting this decrease were a 280 basis point decline from higher commodity and wage inflation and a 50 basis point decline from higher acquisition and divestiture charges, partially offset by a 260 basis point increase from higher sales.
>
> Labor shortages persist broadly in select markets, and shortages of certain raw materials have continued to affect the prices that our businesses are charged, particularly commodities.
>

## Quanta Services Inc. (PWR)

Quanta Services provides specialty contracting and infrastructure services for the electric power grid, power generation, large load centers such as data centers, communications and pipelines, mainly in the United States.

Source: [10-K filed 2026-02-19](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050915/000105091526000006/pwr-20251231.htm)

**Segments**

- **Electric**: Services for the electric power grid, power generation and large load center markets (includes renewable energy infrastructure). Demand: Utilities, renewable developers, technology companies, data center and other large load customers
- **Underground and Infrastructure**: Infrastructure solutions for transportation, distribution, storage and processing of natural gas, oil and other products, and for large load centers. Demand: Pipeline, gas utility and energy delivery customers, and large load center owners

**Geographic exposure.** Operations are primarily in the United States; foreign operations (mainly Canada and Australia) were about 7.0% of 2025 revenues, down from 8.7% in 2024 and 14.2% in 2023.
> We operate primarily in the United States; however, we derived approximately 7.0%, 8.7% and 14.2% of our revenues from foreign operations, primarily in Canada and Australia, during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023.
>
> customers, which primarily include utilities, renewable energy developers, technology companies, communications providers, industrial companies and energy delivery companies located primarily in the United States, Canada and Australia.
>

**Customers.** Customers are utilities, renewable developers, technology companies, communications providers, industrial and energy delivery companies; work comes under master service agreements and fixed and non-fixed price contracts. Customer base is moderately concentrated.
Concentration: Largest customer 8% of 2025 consolidated revenues; ten largest customers 30%.
> For the year ended December 31, 2025, our largest customer accounted for 8% of our consolidated revenues and our ten largest customers accounted for 30% of our consolidated revenues.
>
> Our services are typically provided pursuant to master service agreements (MSAs), repair and maintenance contracts and fixed price and non-fixed price construction and engineering contracts.
>

**Order backlog.** RPO covers firm fixed-price orders and some unit-price work; backlog adds estimated orders under MSAs and short-term non-fixed price contracts.
Latest: Remaining performance obligations $23.76 billion and backlog $43.98 billion at December 31, 2025.
Horizon: 66.1% of RPO expected to be recognized in the subsequent twelve months.
> Our remaining performance obligations and backlog were $23.76 billion and $43.98 billion as of December 31, 2025, representing increases of 41.8%, and 27.3% relative to December 31, 2024.
>
> with 66.1 % and 67.1 % expected to be recognized in the subsequent twelve months
>

**Pricing dynamics.** A significant portion of revenue comes from unit price or fixed price agreements, where price is often a key factor in award; change orders and claims are recognized when a price adjustment is probable.
> A significant portion of our revenues is currently derived from unit price or fixed price agreements, and price is often an important factor in the award of such agreements.
>
> In addition, we recognize amounts associated with change orders and/or claims as revenue when it is probable that the contract price will be adjusted and the amount of any such adjustment can be reasonably estimated.
>

**Margin drivers.** Segment margins rose on higher revenue (fixed cost absorption) and mix of work including acquired businesses; in 2024 mix toward higher-margin emergency restoration helped. Tariffs and sourcing limits mainly threaten project timing.
> primarily due to increased revenues, which contributed to higher levels of fixed cost absorption, as well as overall mix of work performed during the period including from the acquired businesses
>
> The increase in operating income and operating margin for the year ended December 31, 2024 was primarily due to the increase in revenues and change in the overall mix of work, including an increase in higher margin emergency restoration services.
>
> We may continue to be impacted by sourcing restrictions, including, but not limited to, taxes, tariffs and duties, which may negatively impact project timing within certain of our markets in the future.
>

## Bloom Energy Corporation (BE)

Bloom Energy manufactures solid oxide fuel cell Energy Servers that generate on-site electricity, plus electrolyzers for hydrogen, selling to financiers, strategic partners, distributors and end customers with a focus on data centers and critical operations.

Source: [10-K filed 2026-02-09](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1664703/000162828026006516/be-20251231.htm)

**Segments**

- **Bloom Energy (single reportable segment)**: Bloom Energy Server fuel cell systems, installation, operations and maintenance services, electricity under power purchase agreements, and the Bloom Electrolyzer. Demand: Data centers and AI infrastructure, utilities and industrial or commercial customers needing resilient distributed power

**Geographic exposure.** Heavily US-weighted (81% of 2025 revenue, up from 74% in 2024 and 70% in 2023). South Korea is the second-largest market through distribution partnerships; Europe and Asia are small but growing.
> In the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, total revenue in the U.S. was 81 %, 74 % and 70 %, respectively, of our total revenue.
>
> South Korea is our second-largest market, where we began commercial operations in 2018 and have grown our footprint to nearly 682 MW of deployed systems, supported by distribution partnerships with SK ecoplant Co., Ltd. and SK eternix Co., Ltd.
>

**Customers.** Sells to financiers, strategic partners, distributors and direct end users. Revenue is highly concentrated, including a related party customer; a 2025 Brookfield partnership provides project financing for AI infrastructure.
Concentration: Three customers/distributors were about 43%, 13% and 12% of 2025 total revenue (the first is a related party).
> We sell to financiers, strategic partners, distributors and directly to end user customers, all of whom we consider to be a customer.
>
> During the year ended December 31, 2025, revenue from three of these customers and distributors, the first of which is related party, accounted for approximately 43%, 13% and 12% of our total revenue.
>
> In August 2025, we entered into a strategic partnership with Brookfield to support the long-term growth of our fuel cell business and accelerate deployment of clean energy solutions with a focus on powering AI infrastructure.
>

**Order backlog.** The filing defines product backlog and service backlog but the text searched gives no dollar amount or timing; it notes that deploying backlog depends on securing project financing.
Latest: not disclosed.
Horizon: not disclosed.
> We view product backlog as the revenue attributable to existing contractual commitments for the purchase or use of Energy Servers by a financier or an end customer in the future.
>
> Additionally, our ability to deploy our backlog is directly tied to our ability to secure project financing, which is often an unpredictable process.
>

**Pricing dynamics.** Customer pricing is not discussed in detail. The filing describes multi-year supply agreements for pricing stability, past raw material price increases, fixed-price installation risk and tariff mitigation initiatives.
> We have multi-year supply agreements with some of our supply partners for supply continuity and pricing stability.
>
> We have enacted multiple initiatives to mitigate the impact of trade tariffs and other trade protection measures to our cost and supply availability.
>
> Our financial results depend on the execution of customer projects and the timely installation of our products, which may be on a fixed price basis, subjecting us to the risk of cost overruns or other unforeseen expenses in the installation process.
>

**Margin drivers.** Total gross margin was 29% in 2025 vs 27% in 2024 (product 35% vs 37%; service 10% vs minus 1%; electricity 46% vs 26%). Gross profit growth was driven by product demand tied to a hyperscaler project and service improvement; tariffs were not material to gross margin in 2025.
> The increase was predominantly driven by (1) a $139.1 million increase in product gross profit, (2) a $24.3 million improvement in service gross profit (loss)
>
> for fiscal year 2025 the impact of tariffs on our gross margin was not material and currently we do not believe such impacts will be material for fiscal year 2026
>

## Hubbell Incorporated (HUBB)

Hubbell makes electrical and utility products, including grid transmission and distribution components, smart meters and communications and controls, wiring devices and electrical products sold to utilities, contractors and industrial customers mostly through distributors.

Source: [10-K filed 2026-02-12](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/48898/000162828026007500/hubb-20251231.htm)

**Segments**

- **Utility Solutions**: Components that let the grid transmit and distribute energy, plus communications and controls (smart meters, protection and control devices). Demand: Electric utilities (63% of consolidated revenue in 2025), sold primarily through distributors or directly to utilities
- **Electrical Solutions**: Wiring devices, connector and grounding products, other electrical equipment and industrial controls and communication systems. Demand: Non-residential, light and heavy industrial, data center, electric transmission and distribution and renewables markets

**Geographic exposure.** International operations were about 7% of 2025 net sales, so the business is predominantly US based. A regional split is not given in the text searched.
> Our international operations accounted for approximatel y 7% of our Net sales in 2025.
>
> We manufacture and source products and materials from various countries throughout the world.
>

**Customers.** Extensive base of distributors, wholesalers, utilities, OEMs, contractors, telecom companies and retail outlets. Sales are mainly through electrical and industrial distributors and directly to utilities.
Concentration: not disclosed.
> We have an extensive customer base of distributors, wholesalers, electric utilities, OEMs, electrical contractors, telecommunications companies and retail and hardware outlets.
>
> The products are sold into these markets primarily through distributors, or directly to utilities.
>
> Products of the Electrical Solutions segment are sold under various brands and/or trademarks and are primarily sold through electrical and industrial distributors, home centers, retail and hardware outlets, and residential product oriented internet sites.
>

**Order backlog.** Backlog of orders believed firm rose about 14%; most revenue comes from inventoried or short-lead-time products so backlog is not the main driver.
Latest: $2,159 million at December 31, 2025 (vs $1,898 million at December 31, 2024).
Horizon: Substantially all Electrical Solutions backlog expected to ship in 2026; Utility Solutions timing not stated.
> The backlog of orders believed to be firm at December 31, 2025 was $2,159 million compared to $1,898 million at December 31, 2024.
>
> Substantially all of the backlog existing at December 31, 2025 in the Electrical Solutions segment is expected to be shipped to customers in 2026.
>

**Pricing dynamics.** Pricing actions are a stated strategy to offset raw material, component, logistics and tariff cost inflation. In 2025 organic sales growth was on favorable price realization and higher unit volumes.
> Our strategy is to also increase selling prices to offset rising costs of raw materials, components and logistics and supply chain matters when necessary.
>
> We have had to take various pricing actions to cover the increase in our costs associated with inflationary pressure and protect our margin profile.
>
> In 2025, Net sales increased by 3.8% or $216 million and organic Net sales (1) increased by $186 million on favorable price realization and higher unit volumes, as further discussed in segment results below.
>

**Margin drivers.** Operating margin rose 130 bp in 2025 (adjusted 80 bp) on favorable price realization and operational productivity; Electrical Solutions margin was 19.3%, up 150 bp. Pricing and productivity programs are meant to offset inflation and tariffs.
> Operating margin increased in 2025, by 130 basis points and adjusted operating margin (1) increased by 80 basis points, driven by favorable price realization and improved operational productivity.
>
> Our pricing and productivity programs are intended to mitigate the risk to our operating margins related to these inflationary pressures and cost increases as a result of tariffs.
>
> Operating income of the Electrical Solutions segment in 2025 was $418.9 million and increased approximately 15.9% compared to 2024, while operating margin in 2025 increased by 150 basis points to 19.3%.
>

## Powell Industries Inc. (POWL)

Powell develops, designs, manufactures and services custom-engineered electrical equipment and systems that distribute, control and monitor electrical energy, sold mainly to oil and gas and petrochemical, electric utility, and commercial and industrial customers (fiscal year ends September 30).

Source: [10-K filed 2026-11-17](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/80420/000008042026000143/powl-20260930.htm)

**Segments**

- **Powell (one reportable segment)**: Custom-engineered switchgear and power distribution systems, motor and transformer protection, spare parts, retrofit components and services. Demand: Oil and gas and petrochemical, electric utility (generation and distribution), and commercial and other industrial (commercial construction, data centers, metals and mining, pulp and paper)

**Geographic exposure.** Fiscal 2026 revenue was $1,026.2 million domestic and $230.0 million international; projects outside the US were about 18% of consolidated revenue.
> Revenues associated with projects located outside of the United States accounted for approximately 18% of our consolidated revenues in Fiscal 2026.
>
> Domestic revenue increased by 17%, or $146.0 million, to $1,026.2 million, while international revenue increased 3%, or $5.9 million, to $230.0 million in Fiscal 2026.
>

**Customers.** A wide variety of customers and governmental agencies across industrial, utility and commercial markets, with work typically awarded in competitive bids. No single customer exceeded 10% of revenue.
Concentration: No single customer above 10% of consolidated revenues in Fiscal 2026 or Fiscal 2025.
> In both Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025, no single customer accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated revenues.
>
> We market and sell our products and services, which are typically awarded in competitive bid situations, to a wide variety of customers and governmental agencies spanning diverse markets and geographic regions.
>
> In the commercial and other industrial markets, we provide products and services to customers engaged in commercial construction, data centers, metals and mining, pulp and paper, as well as other industrial applications.
>

**Order backlog.** Backlog nearly doubled and excludes service and maintenance contracts billed as performed; it is recognized as remaining performance obligations are completed.
Latest: $2.7 billion at September 30, 2026 (vs $1.4 billion at September 30, 2025).
Horizon: About $1.3 billion (roughly 48%) expected to be recognized in the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027.
> Our backlog increased by $1.3 billion to $2.7 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.4 billion at September 30, 2025.
>
> We anticipate that approximately $1.3 billion of Fiscal 2026 ending backlog will be recognized as revenue during our fiscal year ending September 30, 2027.
>
> Our backlog does not include service and maintenance-type contracts for which we have the right to invoice as services are performed.
>

**Pricing dynamics.** Projects are priced through competitive bids; the company manages pricing, delivery schedules and bid validity dates and uses contract pricing adjustments, estimating and hedging to manage commodity volatility. Fiscal 2026 was described as a stable pricing environment.
> In response to the increased cost environment and supply chain challenges, we strive to effectively manage our product pricing, delivery schedules and bid validity dates with our customers, as well as improve factory efficiencies and project execution.
>
> While the cost outlook for commodities used in the production of our products is not certain, we believe we can manage this volatility through contract pricing adjustments, material-cost predictive estimating, hedging and by active pursuit of internal cost reduction efforts.
>
> The competitive factors used during bid evaluation by our customers vary from project to project and may include technical support and application expertise, engineering and manufacturing capabilities, equipment rating, delivered value, scheduling and price.
>

**Margin drivers.** Gross margin rose to 31% in Fiscal 2026 from 29%, driven by higher revenue, volume leverage, product mix and strong project execution in a stable pricing environment. Tariffs are flagged as a risk; no quantified tariff effect found.
> Gross profit as a percentage of revenue increased to 31% in Fiscal 2026, as compared to 29% in Fiscal 2025.
>
> The increase in gross profit was primarily driven by higher revenues, as well as improved gross profit margin resulting from favorable volume leverage and product mix, as well as strong project execution in a stable pricing environment.
>
> Additional restrictions or economic disincentives on United States or international trade such as significant increases in tariffs on goods could adversely impact our business.
>

## Modine (Modexus Solutions) (MOD)

Modexus Solutions (formerly Modine Manufacturing) sells thermal management solutions, systems, services and components for data center, commercial HVAC&R, commercial vehicle, off-highway and other industrial markets (fiscal year ends March 31).

Source: [10-K filed 2026-05-27](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/67347/000110465926066795/mod-20260331x10k.htm)

**Segments**

- **Climate Solutions**: Data center cooling solutions, HVAC&R heat exchangers and energy-efficient climate-controlled solutions, and anti-corrosive coatings. Demand: Hyperscale and colocation data centers, commercial HVAC&R and buildings (reorganized into Data Centers and Commercial HVAC segments effective April 1, 2026)
- **Performance Technologies**: Heat exchange and thermal products and solutions for vehicular, stationary power and industrial applications (Heavy-Duty Equipment and On-Highway Applications groups). Demand: Commercial vehicle, off-highway, power generation and zero-emission and hybrid vehicles

**Geographic exposure.** Operations span North America, Europe, Asia and India; US export sales were 6 percent of net sales in fiscal 2026. Management expects strong data center growth in North America and Asia, and power generation demand grew in North America, Europe and India.
> Export sales from the U.S. to foreign countries, as a percentage of consolidated net sales, were 6 percent in fiscal 2026 and 7 percent in both fiscal 2025 and 2024.
>
> In North America, we expect the data center markets will experience strong growth, benefitting from significant capital investments in data center infrastructure in the U.S. by both Hyperscale and NeoCloud data center providers.
>
> In Asia, we anticipate the data center markets will experience strong growth in fiscal 2027, driven by AI and high-performance computing demand.
>

**Customers.** Customers are concentrated in data center, commercial vehicle and off-highway markets and are served mainly through long-term sales agreements typically lasting three to five years.
Concentration: Ten largest customers 49 percent of fiscal 2026 net sales.
> Our top five customers, in terms of sales, are in the data center, commercial vehicle, and off-highway markets and our ten largest customers accounted for 49 percent of our net sales in fiscal 2026.
>
> The higher Climate Solutions segment sales included significant sales growth to hyperscale and colocation data center customers and $119 million of incremental sales from businesses we acquired during fiscal 2026.
>
> When it is in the mutual interest of Modine and our customers, we utilize long-term sales agreements to minimize investment risks and provide the customer with a proven source of competitively-priced products.
>

**Order backlog.** The Backlog of Orders section gives no backlog amount; it says segment teams manage production capacity based on expected sales volume.
Latest: not disclosed.
Horizon: not disclosed.
> Our operating segments maintain their own inventories and production schedules.
>
> We believe that our segment teams can manage their operations and production capacity effectively and efficiently based upon expected sales volume in fiscal 2027 and beyond.
>

**Pricing dynamics.** Long-term customer contracts include, when possible, prospective price adjustments tied to key raw material costs, with a lag of three months to a year; metals pricing with suppliers is adjusted monthly or quarterly.
> When possible, we have included provisions within our long-term customer contracts which provide for adjustments to customer prices, on a prospective basis, based upon increases and decreases in the cost of key raw materials.
>
> In addition, there can often be a three-month to one-year lag until the time that the price adjustments take effect.
>
> We typically adjust metals pricing with our raw material suppliers on a monthly basis and our major fabricated component suppliers on a quarterly basis.
>

**Margin drivers.** Fiscal 2026 gross margin fell 190 bp to 23.0 percent on operating inefficiencies from the rapid Data Centers expansion, higher material costs and the absence of prior-year pricing settlements and sales tax credits, even as volume rose 23 percent.
> Gross margin declined 190 basis points to 23.0 percent and was negatively impacted by temporary operating inefficiencies associated with the rapid expansion of our Data Centers business and higher material costs in both of our operating segments.
>
> primarily due to temporary operating inefficiencies, higher material costs, and the absence of commercial pricing settlements and sales tax credits, which favorably impacted the prior year
>
> Cost of sales increased $510 million, or 26 percent, primarily due to the higher sales volume.
>

## Cummins Inc. (CMI)

Cummins designs, manufactures, distributes and services engines, power generation systems, drivetrain and aftertreatment components, and electrified power systems. It sells to OEMs, distributors, dealers and other customers worldwide.

Source: [10-K filed 2026-02-10](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/26172/000002617226000009/cmi-20251231.htm)

**Segments**

- **Engine**: Diesel, natural gas and gasoline engines (15 liters and smaller) and associated parts.. Demand: Heavy-duty truck, medium-duty truck and bus, light-duty automotive (pick-up and light commercial vehicle) and off-highway markets such as construction, agriculture, mining, marine, rail, oil and gas and defense.
- **Components**: Axles, drivelines, brakes and suspension, aftertreatment systems, turbochargers, fuel systems, valvetrain technologies, automated transmissions and electronics.. Demand: Commercial vehicle and industrial applications, OEM first fit and retrofit customers, and aftermarket sold to OEM dealers, independent distributors and service garages.
- **Distribution**: Wholesaling of engines, generator sets and service parts, plus service and repair on Cummins products and aftermarket support for Accelera.. Demand: Customers and certified dealers worldwide through seven geographic regions; the segment is the primary sales, service and support channel.
- **Power Systems**: Standby and prime power generators, engines (16 liters and larger) for generator sets and industrial applications, alternators and other power components.. Demand: Highly diversified customer groups; industrial uses include mining, oil and gas, marine, rail and defense; 2025 growth was in power generation, especially data center and commercial markets.
- **Accelera**: Electrified power systems with components and subsystems, including battery and electric powertrain technologies.. Demand: Highly diversified, multiple end markets as they adopt electric solutions; segment is in early stages of commercializing.

**Geographic exposure.** International sales (excluding the U.S. and Canada) were 40% of 2025 net sales versus 39% in 2024. In 2025 U.S. and Canada sales declined 3% while international sales rose 2%, led by China and Europe.
> Sales to international markets (excluding the U.S. and Canada), based on location of customers, were 40 percent of total net sales in 2025, compared with 39 percent of total net sales in 2024.
>
> International sales (excludes the U.S. and Canada) improved by 2 percent, primarily due to higher sales in China and Europe, partially offset by lower sales in Latin America.
>
> China, India, Europe, Asia Pacific, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa are our largest geographic markets outside of North America
>

**Customers.** Thousands of customers worldwide, with a few large truck OEMs under long-term supply agreements (PACCAR, Traton, Daimler, Stellantis); distribution through a wholly-owned, partially-owned and independent distributor and dealer network.
Concentration: PACCAR 13% of 2025 consolidated net sales (about $4.4 billion; 16% in 2024 and 2023), the only customer above 10%; PACCAR, Traton, Daimler and Stellantis together 31% of 2025 net sales..
> PACCAR is our largest customer, accounting for 13 percent of our consolidated net sales in 2025, 16 percent in 2024 and 16 percent in 2023.
>
> Collectively, our net sales to these four customers, including PACCAR, were 31 percent of our consolidated net sales in 2025, 36 percent in 2024 and 37 percent in 2023.
>
> We sell our products to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), distributors, dealers and other customers worldwide.
>

**Order backlog.** The 10-K gives no backlog amount. It says much of the business runs on open purchase orders that are not considered firm, and that data center product demand extends six to eight quarters.
Latest: not disclosed.
Horizon: not disclosed.
> Many of these open orders are historically subject to month-to-month releases and are subject to cancellation on reasonable notice without cancellation charges and therefore are not considered firm.
>
> We also have strong demand for our data center products extending out six to eight quarters.

**Pricing dynamics.** Prices follow contractual time frames with pricing adjustment provisions, but timing of commodity cost increases can prevent timely pass-through. In 2025 non-tariff pricing (light-duty automotive engine launches) and customer tariff recoveries helped revenue, and favorable pricing lifted Engine, Distribution and Power Systems EBITDA; net tariff impact was immaterial.
> Our businesses establish prices with our customers in accordance with contractual time frames; however, the timing of material and commodity market price increases may prevent us from passing these additional costs on to our customers through timely pricing actions.
>
> Power Systems segment EBITDA increased $514 million, primarily due to favorable pricing and higher volumes, partially offset by net tariff costs.
>

> Distribution segment EBITDA increased $430 million, primarily due to increased power generation volumes in North America, improved mix, favorable pricing, decreased compensation expenses, lower material costs and improved operational leverage.

> We primarily operate in the United States and Canada, and have a smaller presence in Europe, Australia and New Zealand.

**Customers.** Highly diversified customer base across construction and industrial end markets; equipment is rented through a branch network supported by a national account sales force and an online rental platform. Credit concentration is low.

**Order backlog.** The 10-K does not report a backlog or remaining performance obligations. The only forward-looking balance is deferred revenue of $175 million at December 31, 2025 ($185 million in 2024).
Latest: not disclosed.
Horizon: not disclosed.

**Pricing dynamics.** Rental pricing shows up in fleet productivity, which combines rental rates, time utilization and mix (up 2.2% in 2025, 2.0% pro forma for Yak). Part of inflationary cost increases, mainly fuel and delivery, is passed on to customers, and tariffs could raise costs beyond what is recovered.
> fleet productivity is a comprehensive metric that reflects the combined impact of changes in rental rates, time utilization, and mix that contribute to the variance in owned equipment rental revenue.
>
> Equipment rentals increased 6.0 percent, primarily due to a 2.2 percent increase in fleet productivity, which includes the impact of the Yak acquisition, and a 3.9 percent increase in average OEC.

> A portion of inflationary cost increases is passed on to customers. The most significant cost increases that are passed on to customers are for fuel and delivery, and there are other costs for which the pass through to customers is less direct

> Gross margin decreased primarily due to 1) increased depreciation expense, including the impact of the Yak acquisition and growth in the acquired Yak locations, 2) inflation and normal cost variability, particularly in delivery costs
>

## MasTec Inc. (MTZ)

MasTec is a North American infrastructure contractor providing engineering, construction, installation and maintenance for communications, power delivery, clean energy and pipeline customers. Much of its work is under multi-year master service agreements; the rest is project-based.

Source: [10-K filed 2026-02-26](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/15615/000001561526000020/mtz-20251231.htm)

**Segments**

- **Communications**: Engineering, construction, maintenance and customer fulfillment for wireless and wireline/fiber networks, data center buildout and interconnection, and install-to-the-home services.. Demand: Communications and digital infrastructure customers; demand tied to fiber expansion, wireless densification and broadband deployment.
- **Clean Energy and Infrastructure**: Installation and construction of power generation facilities (wind, solar, biomass, natural gas, hydrogen), battery storage, heavy civil and industrial infrastructure, and environmental remediation.. Demand: Energy, utility, government and other end markets; segment revenue about $4.7 billion in 2025.
- **Power Delivery**: Engineering, construction and maintenance of transmission and distribution infrastructure, substations, grid modernization and emergency restoration.. Demand: Energy, utility and data center infrastructure industries; driven by electricity demand growth, grid reliability and aging grid.
- **Pipeline Infrastructure**: Construction, maintenance and integrity services for natural gas, water, wastewater and carbon capture sequestration pipelines.. Demand: Energy and utility customers; demand sensitive to oil and gas activity and industrial and utility demand.
- **Other**: Certain equity investees and small business units with activities in international end markets.. Demand: International end markets; not a primary segment.

**Geographic exposure.** Revenue is primarily from North America; international revenue is a small portion, with foreign operations primarily in Canada.
> We derive a small portion of our revenue from international markets.
>
> Our foreign operations are presently conducted primarily in Canada, but we have performed work in various other foreign countries in the past and may expand our foreign operations in the future.
>
> All five reportable segments derive their revenue primarily from the engineering, installation and maintenance of infrastructure, primarily in North America.
>

**Customers.** About 1,800 customers, including large communications, utility, power and pipeline companies, with work won mostly through bids. Master service and other service agreements (generally multi-year, cancelable on short notice) were 44% of 2025 revenue.
Concentration: Top ten customers 34% of 2025 revenue (35% in 2024, 38% in 2023); one customer about 10% of net accounts receivable at December 31, 2025; no single-customer revenue percentage in the evidence pack..
> The Company had approximately 1,800 customers for the year ended December 31, 2025.
>
> For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Company derived 34 %, 35 % and 38 %, respectively, of its revenue from its top ten customers.
>
> For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, revenue derived from projects performed under master service and other service agreements totaled 44%, 41% and 40%, respectively, of consolidated revenue.
>

**Order backlog.** Backlog covers 18 months and includes master service agreement estimates, so it exceeds remaining performance obligations; 47% of backlog is under MSAs that carry no minimum purchase commitment.
Latest: 18-month estimated backlog $18,963 million at December 31, 2025; remaining performance obligations $14.6 billion at December 31, 2025..
Horizon: About 74% of year-end 2025 backlog expected to be realized in 2026; about $9.3 billion, or 63.7%, of remaining performance obligations expected in 2026..
> Estimated backlog represents the amount of revenue we expect to realize over the next 18 months from future work on uncompleted construction contracts, including new contracts under which work has not begun, as well as revenue from change orders and renewal options.
>
> we anticipate that we will realize approximately 74% of our estimated year-end 2025 backlog in 2026.
>
> Based on current expectations, the Company anticipates it will recognize approximately $ 9.3 billion, or 63.7 %, of its remaining performance obligations as revenue during 2026
>
> As of December 31, 2025, 47% of our backlog is estimated to be attributable to amounts under master service or other service agreements, pursuant to which our customers are not contractually committed to purchase a minimum amount of services.
>

**Pricing dynamics.** Customers award most work through bids where price is often a principal factor; much revenue is fixed price or per unit, so cost overruns hit margins. Inflation in labor, materials and fuel hurts profitability to the extent costs cannot be passed through.
> they award most of their work through a bid process, and price is often a principal factor in determining which service provider is selected.
>
> We derive a significant portion of our revenue from fixed price master service and other service agreements.
>
> Elevated levels of labor, fuel and material costs have in the past and could in the future negatively affect our project margins to the extent that we are unable to pass such cost increases along to our customers.
>

**Margin drivers.** Cost of revenue rose to 87.5% of revenue in 2025 from 86.8% on reduced project efficiencies and mix in Pipeline Infrastructure and Power Delivery, partly offset by better productivity in Clean Energy and Infrastructure. The filing also names job productivity, weather, labor and material costs, and geographic mix.
> Costs of revenue, excluding depreciation and amortization, as a percentage of revenue increased by approximately 70 basis points to 87.5% of revenue in 2025 compared to 86.8% of revenue in 2024.
>
> The basis point increase was due to a combination of reduced project efficiencies and project mix, primarily within our Pipeline Infrastructure and Power Delivery segments
>
> Overall project margins may fluctuate due to project pricing and job conditions, changes in the cost of labor and materials, crew availability, job productivity and work volume.
>

Rockwell Automation sells industrial automation hardware, software, solutions and services (drives, motion, controls, safety, software, digital and lifecycle services) to manufacturers worldwide. Fiscal 2026 ended September 30, 2026.

Source: [10-K filed 2026-11-12](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1024478/000102447826000048/rok-20260930.htm)

**Segments**

EV and battery, semiconductor, e-commerce and warehouse automation), hybrid (food and beverage, household and personal care, life sciences) and process (energy, mining, chemicals).

**Geographic exposure.** Sales outside the U.S. were less than half of fiscal 2026 sales; U.S. sales were $5,381 million in 2026. Largest non-U.S. markets are Canada, China, Italy, the United Kingdom and Mexico.

>

>
> Sales in North America include $ 5,381 million, $ 4,847 million, and $ 4,612 million related to the U.S. in 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively.
>

**Customers.** Manufacturers across discrete, hybrid and process industries. In most countries ROK sells primarily through independent distributors plus a direct sales force; large systems and services go mainly through the direct sales force.
Concentration: Each of the three largest distributors about 10% of 2026 total sales, about 30% combined (all three operating segments)..
> In most countries, we sell primarily through independent distributors in conjunction with our direct sales force.
>
> Sales to each of our three largest distributors represented approximately 10 percent of our total sales in 2026, and collectively, sales to these three distributors represented approximately 30 percent of our total sales.
>
> Major markets served by all segments consist of discrete end markets (e.g., Automotive including Electric Vehicle and Battery, Semiconductor, and e-Commerce & Warehouse Automation)
>

**Order backlog.** Only remaining performance obligations are reported, excluding contracts of one year or less and contracts billed as performed, so it covers a small part of annual sales.
Latest: About $1,370 million at September 30, 2026..
Horizon: About $785 million expected to be recognized over the next 12 months; remainder thereafter..
> As of September 30, 2026, we expect to recognize approximately $ 1,370 million of revenue in future periods from unfulfilled performance obligations from existing contracts with customers.
>
> We expect to recognize revenue of approximately $ 785 million from our remaining performance obligations over the next 12 months with the remaining balance recognized thereafter.
>
> We have applied the practical expedient to exclude the value of remaining performance obligations for (i) contracts with an original term of one year or less
>

**Pricing dynamics.** ROK manages tariff costs through pricing and supply chain actions and expects them to mostly offset tariff costs, but recovery can lag. Fiscal 2026 results include price realization, an $85 million sales reduction for a customer refund program tied to IEEPA tariff price increases, and IEEPA tariff refunds received.
> We continue to manage the impact of tariffs through pricing and other supply chain actions, including the use of alternative sources of materials and redundant manufacturing locations.
>
> In September 2026, we approved and communicated a refund program for customers who paid price increases on purchases of products that were impacted by IEEPA tariffs.
>
> We estimated the expected value of tariff refunds to be issued to customers under the refund program and recognized an accrual of $ 85 million as a reduction of sales in the Consolidated Statement of Operations for the year ended September 30, 2026.
>

**Margin drivers.** Enterprise operating margin rose to 22.2% in fiscal 2026 from 18.9% on higher volume, price realization, favorable mix, productivity and net IEEPA tariff refund items, partly offset by higher compensation. Intelligent Devices segment margin rose to 20.0% from 18.0%.
> Enterprise operating margin was 22.2 percent in 2026 compared to 18.9 percent in 2025.
>
> The increases were primarily due to higher sales volume, price realization, favorable mix, productivity, and the net impact of IEEPA tariff refund related items, partially offset by higher compensation.
>
> Segment operating margin increased to 20.0 percent in 2026 from 18.0 percent in 2025, primarily due to higher sales volume, productivity, and favorable mix, partially offset by higher compensation.
>

>

**Pricing dynamics.** Pricing actions to offset material, labor and transportation inflation accounted for almost half of Electrification revenue growth in 2023 and around three quarters in 2022; some contracts carry raw-material price escalation clauses, and ABB cannot always pass costs on.
> Pricing actions taken to mitigate increasing material, labor and transportation costs again contributed strongly to the higher revenue level and accounted for almost half of the revenue growth in 2023
>
> in some cases we can reduce this risk by incorporating changes in raw materials prices into the prices of our end products (through price escalation clauses)
>
> All Business areas reported revenue growth, with both increased volumes and product prices.
>

**Margin drivers.** Motion and Electrification profit gains in 2023 came from volume, backlog execution and pricing that more than offset labor and material inflation; Process Automation also cites favorable mix and project execution. E-mobility losses included inventory charges.
> The increase was driven by higher revenues reflecting a strong demand, solid order backlog execution and benefits from a strong price execution which more than offset cost inflation related to labor and materials.
>
> Growth was driven by higher revenue volumes, continued operational improvements in project execution and a favorable business mix.
>
> including the mandatory target to make annual productivity improvements of at least 3-5 percent each year
>
